telegramBot.finding: No direct LUMI workflow exists; raw AI advice must not be presented as payment authority.

site.finding: The shadow operator advisory does not require a customer-site surface.

miniApp.finding: The shadow operator advisory does not require a customer Mini App surface.

admin.finding: The separate KAIROS operator UI exposes committee/provider controls and truthfully says AI cannot bypass numeric gates, but lacks a bounded LUMI verdict/review, egress, model, failure and retention view.

api.finding: A live shared-token KAIROS-to-LUMI generic resolver bridge and operator committee APIs exist beside a safer dormant frozen shadow wire; the live path is not the canonical E2 contract.

native.finding: LUMI advisory must not receive native keys or signing authority and needs no native surface.

authorityFinding.reason: KAIROS records the committee/LUMI result, then unconditionally evaluates its own execution path; the advisory return is ignored.
authorityFinding.misleadingContract: The generic LUMI resolver can emit APPROVE with actionAllowed=true even though the result neither authorizes nor vetoes KAIROS execution.

positiveControls: The live bridge is loopback-only, uses a dedicated minimum-length shared bearer and LUMI verifies it with constant-time comparison for exactly two POST paths.
Malformed or failed external committee output becomes ABSTAIN and the arbiter can only tighten the committee result.
The frozen shadow wire bounds and hashes requests, correlates responses and maps timeout, error or malformed response to HOLD with action false.
The frozen LUMI adapter rejects identity-, credential- and money-like facts and uses a closed signal catalog.
Effective service units use dedicated non-root users and strong filesystem, capability and loopback network restrictions.

riskFindings.finding: Production uses generic /conflict/resolve rather than the bounded ALLOW/HOLD/MANUAL/FREEZE frozen E2 wire, so request correlation, replay protection, signed response receipts and strict fail-closed semantics are absent.

On bridge error combinedVerdict falls back to the committee verdict, including possible APPROVE; KAIROS currently ignores it, but the documented fail-closed claim is false and unsafe for future gating.
KAIROS executes an eligible candidate after recording advisory without consuming combinedVerdict, so LUMI cannot currently provide the E2 tightening/veto gate.
The actual static-bearer path has no nonce, freshness, idempotency, replay ledger or route-specific throttle; generic task/output dictionaries have no explicit size/depth bounds.
The bridge sends route/symbol label, exact net percentage/value and all role/vote/confidence/free-text reasons; no exact classification or bounded minimization contract governs the live payload.

Generic audit is process-memory, host registration is a best-effort mutation, KAIROS keeps a capped count-based memory file, and no accepted content-bound durable audit, time retention, deletion or backup-expiry contract exists.
Prior production inventory found one verified external Cerebras provider filling uncovered committee roles and fallback arbiter, so the apparent committee is not independent.
Operator UI omits LUMI dry-run status, provider egress, non-independent committee composition, combined verdict, failure and retention details.
Bridge stores exception type plus truncated exception text in operator-visible state without a dedicated redaction contract.
Deployed LUMI service-auth main.py matches checkout but both it and its focused service-auth test are untracked, so deployed provenance is not accepted.
